candidates.tagline: NYC spent millions on a protected bike lane that ends at a staircase
candidates.story: In August 2026, NYC DOT opened a new protected bike lane on Riverside Drive in Inwood — designed to connect cyclists to the Hudson River Greenway — but the route dead-ends at a flight of stairs, forcing riders to haul their bikes up on foot; the direct stair-free alternative was rejected by the local community board in 2024 to preserve 40 parking spots.
candidates.why_funny: The city built a 'protected' cycling connection to a greenway that requires abandoning your bike to use, because protecting 40 parking spots was more important than a route cyclists can actually cycle on.
candidates.alt: A cyclist hauling a bicycle up a concrete flight of stairs on Riverside Drive in Inwood, New York City, where the new protected bike lane physically ends at the staircase leading to the Hudson River Greenway

candidates.tagline: Samsung's $1,200 flagship tablet still has the notch users have begged them to remove since 2022
candidates.story: Leaked renders published August 8–11, 2026 confirmed that the upcoming Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra will keep the exact same V-shaped display notch first introduced on the Tab S8 Ultra in 2022 — a design users have criticised as 'unsightly' for four years — while rivals moved to punch-hole or under-display cameras; tech outlets called it 'our worst fears confirmed.'
candidates.why_funny: Samsung spent four years listening to customers beg them to remove the notch from their premium 14.6-inch AMOLED display, then built the exact same notch again and called it a flagship.
candidates.alt: Close-up of the front of a Samsung Galaxy Tab S8 Ultra showing the dual front-facing cameras mounted in the V-shaped notch cutout at the top of the display — the same notch design confirmed to continue in the Tab S12 Ultra
